{"basis":"measured","fact_type":"defect","name":"MEASURED 2026-09-27 on 0.72.0: plan_epoch on an existing epoch with only name and sequence CLEARED its description, despite "omitted fields keep their stored value"","source":"who:claude-code","statement":"MEASURED 2026-09-27 on reflow2 0.72.0 (the dev_reflow2 hub's shared server for reflow2's design), while recording the combined plan. plan_epoch was called on seven existing planned epochs with only `id`, `name` and `sequence`, to renumber them. Each reply echoed name, sequence, epoch_type and status and NO description, and get_node on epoch:planned-a-code-folder-names-its-design confirmed the description was gone. All seven were restored by hand from their earlier get_node reads in the same session; nothing was lost.

The tool description says the opposite: "CONTENT FIELDS ARE REQUIRED TO CREATE AND OPTIONAL TO REVISE: call it again with the same id and only what you are changing — omitted fields keep their stored value".

THE CONVERSE HELD on flo2's server (same version) the same day: plan_epoch on epoch:off-site-backups with only `id` and `description` KEPT its name, sequence and epoch_type. So the observed loss is of `description` when it is omitted, not of every omitted field.

SAME CLASS AS fact:revising-a-finding-resets-its-fact-type-to-finding-2026-09-26 (record_finding reset an omitted fact_type) and the re-declare defect the hub records (external_dependency drops a Resource's description). No cause is asserted here: this records what happened, not why.

WORKAROUND UNTIL FIXED: when revising an epoch, always pass its description, read first with get_node.

UPDATE 2026-09-28: re-measured on a 0.72.0 scratch store during the class sweep. plan_epoch {id, name} cleared BOTH `description` and `checksum`; add_epoch kept both. The mechanism, read in source: core plan_epoch writes with create_node (replace) and carries only `status` forward (the 09-11 instance fix), while add_epoch uses upsert_node.
